atlassian.admin_note:
Saving a key does not install anything on the work computer. If the assistant says the tool is unavailable, write to your administrator — preparing the machine is their job, not yours.
The mcp-atlassian program itself does not need installing: it ships with the app and is unpacked on the computer at first launch.
atlassian.description: Search tasks and read wiki pages in Jira and Confluence.
atlassian.guide:
1. Open {{jiraHost}} → your profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token.
2. Copy the token and paste it into the Jira field.
3. Do the same on {{confluenceHost}} and paste the second token into the Confluence field.
If your Jira and Confluence are Cloud (an *.atlassian.net address), there are no personal access tokens there: create an API token at id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens and fill in the e-mail + API token pair instead of the personal-token fields.
The tool stays off until both fields are filled in.
atlassian.guide_unknown_hosts:
1. Your administrator gives you the Jira and Confluence addresses — ask them if you do not know.
2. Open the Jira address → your profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token, copy the token and paste it into the Jira field.
3. Do the same in Confluence and paste the second token into the Confluence field.
If your Jira and Confluence are Cloud (an *.atlassian.net address), there are no personal access tokens there: create an API token at id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens and fill in the e-mail + API token pair instead of the personal-token fields.
The tool stays off until both fields are filled in.
atlassian.rights: The token acts as you, so the assistant sees exactly what you see and nothing more. No separate permissions have to be granted — but check that you yourself can reach the Jira projects and Confluence spaces you care about: the assistant reads tasks, comments, pages, history and attachments, and moves tasks between statuses. Giving the token an expiry date is a good habit.
atlassian.title: Jira & Confluence
atlassian.verify: Ask the assistant to "show my Jira tasks" and to "find the Confluence page about …". A list back means the key was accepted. If an task you know exists comes back as "nothing found", the token was probably truncated when copied, or has expired: create a new one and paste it again.

outlook.title: Outlook mail & calendar
outlook.description: Read your work mail, search your threads, and check the calendar.
outlook.guide:
1. Enter your work mailbox address — that is the only thing stored here.
2. No password is asked for and none is stored: sign-in uses your work account.
The tool stays off until the address is filled in.
outlook.rights: Access covers exactly your own mailbox and your own calendar. The assistant reads messages, subjects, attachments, meetings and free slots; sending mail is off by default, so it will not write to anyone as you. If you need a shared or delegated mailbox, you have to be granted access to it first.
outlook.verify: Ask "what important mail came in today". A list of messages means it works. If the assistant says the mailbox is unavailable, check the address — usually it is a typo, or a personal alias instead of the primary address.
outlook.admin_note: For mail to connect, the work computer has to be prepared and you have to be signed in to it with your work account. If the assistant reports the mailbox as unavailable, that one is for your administrator.

bitrix24.title: Bitrix24 & knowledge base
bitrix24.description: Deals and comments from CRM, plus corporate knowledge-base search.
bitrix24.webhook_hint: The part after /rest/ in your webhook address — or paste the full webhook URL.
bitrix24.webhook_invalid: The webhook must not contain spaces, ? or #.
bitrix24.guide:
1. In Bitrix24 open your profile → Developer resources → Other → Inbound webhook.
2. Copy the tail of the address — it looks like 123/abc…/ — and paste it into the webhook field.
3. Ask the knowledge-base team for the knowledge-base token; they task the search id together with it, and it is optional.
The tool stays off until the webhook and the token are filled in.
bitrix24.rights: When you create the webhook, tick CRM access — without it the assistant cannot see deals; to let it read a deal's conversation, add access to comments and files as well. A webhook is never broader than your own permissions. The knowledge-base token is read-only.
bitrix24.verify: Ask "show my open deals". A list means the webhook was accepted. A permission error almost always means CRM was not ticked when the webhook was created: make a new one with the right scopes. Then ask it to "find … in the knowledge base" to check the second token.
bitrix24.admin_note: The portal address and the knowledge-base address are set by an administrator while preparing your workplace. If the assistant cannot reach Bitrix24 at all, that one is for them.

fetch.admin_note:
Internet access from the work computer is configured by an administrator. If nothing opens at all, that is the reason — not the toggle.
The mcp-server-fetch program itself does not need installing: it ships with the app and is unpacked on the computer at first launch.
fetch.description: The assistant opens web pages from links you give it.
fetch.guide: No credentials are needed — just flip the toggle. After that the assistant can open web pages you give it links to.
fetch.rights: No keys and no separate permissions are asked of you. The assistant visits only the addresses you name and reads pages the way a browser does: it sends nothing and fills in no forms.
fetch.title: Web access
fetch.verify: Give the assistant any link and ask it to summarise the page. Getting the contents back means it works. If it reports the page as unavailable, that address is most likely blocked by the work network's rules.

mcp_gateway.admin_note: Access itself is set up by the platform team. If the token is accepted but the tools do not answer, that one is for them.
mcp_gateway.admin_note_self_install: If the computer is your own and you have no administrator, the missing program is installed with pipx install mcp-proxy.
mcp_gateway.description: The set of tools your company tasks to you personally.
mcp_gateway.guide:
1. Ask the platform team for your personal corporate gateway token.
2. Paste it into the field below.
The tool stays off while the field is empty.
mcp_gateway.rights: The token is personal: it opens exactly the set of work tools issued to you. Ask for one in your own name — a colleague's token will not work and must not be passed around.
mcp_gateway.title: Extra work tools
mcp_gateway.verify: Ask the assistant to list which tools it currently has. Work tools showing up means the token was accepted. If the gateway refuses, the token has most likely expired: request a new one.
